title: Navigate a project from the menu bar
prompt:
# Story: Navigate a project from the menu bar

- **Story**: XXX-navigation-and-menu-bar
- **Created**: 2026-10-31
- **Status**: Draft

## Story

As a team member, I want a menu bar on the left with the list of my projects above it, so that after I create a
project I land on the main page and can move between the project's pages, and between projects, from one place.

## Acceptance tests

### A. The first visit and creating a project

1. **Given** no project exists, **When** the app opens, **Then** the left bar shows the label "Project" and a selector
   reading "No project yet / Create one to get started"; below it the label "Menu" and the eight menu items, all
   disabled and dimmed; the main area shows "Welcome to BWYN", the text "Create your first project to start feeding
   drivers, reviewing decisions and building.", and a "Create project" button.
2. **Given** any state, **When** the user presses "New project" in the header, in the project dropdown, or "Create
   project" on the welcome page, **Then** a dialog "Create project" opens, with the text "A project groups the drivers,
   decisions and integrations of one product.", a Name field with focus (placeholder "e.g. Payments platform"), an
   optional Description field, and Cancel and "Create project" buttons.
3. **Given** the dialog, **When** the user submits an empty name (or only spaces), **Then** "Give the project a name."
   shows under the field and nothing is created.
4. **Given** a project called "Payments", **When** the user submits "payments " (any case, spaces around), **Then** "A
   project with this name already exists." shows and nothing is created. Typing in the field clears the message.
5. **Given** the dialog, **When** the user presses Escape, the Close (X) button, Cancel, or clicks outside the dialog,
   **Then** it closes and nothing is created.
6. **Given** a valid name, **When** the user presses "Create project", **Then** the dialog closes, the project becomes
   the active one, and the main page shows the Builder page (the builder workspace is closed), with "Builder" selected in
   the menu.

### B. The left bar once a project exists

7. **Given** an active project, **Then** the top of the bar shows "Project" and a selector with the project's avatar
   (its first two letters in capitals, on a coloured square), its name, and "Active project".
8. **Given** the menu, **Then** it shows, in this order, each with an icon: P&P, Builder, Drivers, Architecture, ADR,
   Integrations, Plugins, Settings. All are enabled. The selected one has a light indigo background, a thin indigo bar on
   its left edge and `aria-current="page"`.
9. **Given** the bottom of the bar, **Then** it shows the logo "B", the name "BWYN" and a "Spike" tag.
10. **Given** projects were created, **Then** each new project gets the next colour of a palette of five, starting over
    after the fifth.

### C. Choosing a project

11. **Given** two or more projects, **When** the user presses the selector, **Then** a list opens below it
    (`role="listbox"`) with each project's avatar and name, a check beside the active one, and "New project" at the
    bottom after a divider.
12. **Given** the list is open, **When** the user chooses a project, **Then** the list closes, that project becomes
    active, and the page the user was on stays selected but now shows that project's content.
13. **Given** the list is open, **When** the user presses Escape or clicks anywhere outside it, **Then** it closes and
    nothing changes.
14. **Given** the list is open, **When** the user chooses "New project", **Then** the list closes and the "Create
    project" dialog opens.

### D. Choosing a page

15. **Given** an active project, **When** the user chooses a menu item, **Then** the main area shows that page with a
    short fade, and the item becomes the selected one.
16. **Given** a page, **Then** the top of the main area (the header) shows a folder icon, the project name, a "/" and the
    page's label, for example "Payments / Drivers"; with no project it reads "No project / Builder".
17. **Given** a page other than Settings, **Then** the main area starts with a large icon, the page's title and its
    one-sentence description, as in this table:

    | Menu item | Title | Description |
    |---|---|---|
    | P&P | Principles & Practices | The principles this team holds to, and the Extreme Programming and evolutionary architecture practices it follows. |
    | Builder | Builder | Turn intent into working software, one guided step at a time. |
    | Drivers | Drivers | The forces that steer decisions. Describe each driver and save it: they feed the skills used by the builder. |
    | Architecture | Architecture | The architecture of the system: its style, its layers and the rules between them. Stories are checked against it. |
    | ADR | Architecture decisions | The decision log of this project. |
    | Integrations | External integrations | Connect the tools the project already lives in. |
    | Plugins | Plugins | Extend the builder with extra skills, checks and generators. |
    | Settings | Settings | The settings of this project. |

18. **Given** the application starts with a project, **Then** the Builder page is the one shown first.

### E. The menu makes room for a workspace

19. **Given** the Builder page, **When** the user presses "Open the builder", **Then** the menu bar shrinks to a narrow
    rail of icons: at the top the active project's avatar (tooltip "<project> (expand menu)"), then the eight items as
    icons only with their name as tooltip and accessible name, and at the bottom an "Expand menu" button. The header adds
    "/ Prompt" after "Builder". The workspace fills the rest of the width.
20. **Given** the user opens Settings, **Then** the same rail appears and the page opens with a menu of its own beside
    it.
21. **Given** the rail, **When** the user presses the avatar or "Expand menu", **Then** the full menu returns and a
    "Collapse menu" button appears beside the logo.
22. **Given** the builder workspace is open, **When** the user chooses any other page, **Then** the workspace closes and
    that page opens in a normal width. **When** the user chooses Builder again, **Then** the Builder page opens (not the
    workspace).
23. **Given** the builder workspace is open, **When** the user chooses another project, **Then** the workspace shows the
    new project's files and starts without anything open.

### F. Theme and memory

24. **Given** the header, **Then** a Dark/Light switch (two buttons, the active one pressed) and a "New project"
    button are on its right.
25. **Given** the user chooses a theme, **Then** the whole app changes at once, and the choice is remembered. Dark is the
    default.
26. **Given** the user reloads the browser, **Then** the projects and the active project are still there, and the app
    opens on the Builder page. If the remembered active project no longer exists, the first project is used.
27. **Given** the browser's storage is blocked or holds invalid data, **Then** the app starts empty and never shows an
    error.

## Business rules and constraints

- A project is a name, an optional description, a creation time, an id and a palette index. The name is trimmed and
  must be unique, ignoring case.
- The project selector, the menu and the logo form one left bar. The header and the main area are to its right.
- Menu items are disabled until a project is active, because every page belongs to a project.
- The page shown is keyed by project and page, so nothing from one project can show in another.
- Creating a project always lands on the Builder page, whatever page was open.
- Everything is reachable by keyboard, with a visible focus ring. Dialogs and lists close with Escape. The selector has
  `aria-haspopup="listbox"` and `aria-expanded`.
- The projects, the active project and the theme are kept in the browser only, in this spike.

## Out of scope

- The content of each page (they are other stories), the builder workspace and the Settings menu items.
- Renaming, deleting, archiving or reordering projects, project settings, users, roles and permissions.
- Saving the page the user was on between visits.
- A mobile layout.

## Tasks

- [ ] Hold the projects and the active id in one state with load, create and select, saved to the browser.
- [ ] Build the project selector and the avatar, with the open list and its keyboard and outside-click handling.
- [ ] Build the "Create project" dialog with its two validations.
- [ ] Describe the eight menu items once (id, label, title, description, icon) and draw the menu from that list.
- [ ] Build the left bar: selector, menu with the selected and disabled states, logo.
- [ ] Build the header with the breadcrumb, the theme switch and the New project button.
- [ ] Build the welcome page and the page frame (icon, title, description, fade, keyed by project and page).
- [ ] Add the collapsed rail and the rules that open and close it.
- [ ] Add the theme, applied to the document and remembered.
